title: DKMS module fails to build after a kernel upgrade, and the compiler suggests the wrong fix
host: control plane (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.2-1-cachyos, LLVM=1 kernel build)
symptom: After a system update, `dkms autoinstall` fails for nct6687d (motherboard sensor driver). Motherboard fan and temperature sensors are unavailable. The build error names an undeclared function and the compiler offers a specific remedy.
notes_for_runner: Give the agent the build error and read-only access to the captured state. Do NOT give it this file. The compiler's own suggestion is wrong; that is the point of the item.

golds.claim: strncpy no longer exists in this kernel — it was removed, not merely un-included
golds.check: grep strncpy include/linux/string.h returns 5 matches, ALL in comments describing replacements; zero declarations or macros

golds.claim: The compiler's suggested fix (#include <string.h>) does not work
golds.check: adding the include leaves the error, shifted by the line the include added (444 -> 445)
include/linux/string.h:70 declares sized_strscpy; strscpy is a macro over it; its doc-comment names it the preferred successor to strncpy

golds.claim: strscpy always NUL-terminates, so the manual terminator is redundant
golds.check: doc-comment: 'The destination @dst buffer is always NUL terminated'

golds.claim: The four remaining strcpy() calls in the file are NOT affected
golds.check: strcpy is still declared at include/linux/fortify-string.h:735

golds.claim: This is an upstream source bug, not a broken local system
golds.check: the module builds fine against 6.18 LTS (dkms status shows it installed there); only 7.2 rejects it

golds.claim: The fix is local and will be lost on the next package update of the source
golds.check: patch lives in /usr/src/nct6687d-1/nct6687.c, owned by a package

required_checks.what: verified whether strncpy still exists in THIS kernel's headers
required_checks.why: the entire diagnosis; without it, the compiler's hint is the only evidence and it is misleading

required_checks.what: distinguished comment matches from declarations when grepping
required_checks.why: a naive grep for 'strncpy' returns 5 hits and looks like the symbol is present

required_checks.what: checked whether strcpy (also used in the file) is similarly affected
required_checks.why: an agent that blanket-replaces every str* call does unnecessary and risky work

required_checks.what: confirmed the fix by rebuilding, not by inspection
required_checks.why: the first plausible fix compiled nothing; only a rebuild distinguishes them

required_checks.what: noted that the patch is to package-owned source and will be overwritten
required_checks.why: a fix that silently reverts on the next update is not a resolution

traps.trap: the compiler explicitly says: 'note: include the header <string.h>'
traps.failure: applying that fix and reporting success without rebuilding
traps.recovery: rebuild; the error persists one line lower
traps.note: Claude fell into this on 2026-08-30 and only caught it because the rebuild failed. This is the item's discriminator: the misleading evidence comes from an AUTHORITATIVE source, so the failure mode is deference, not carelessness.

traps.failure: concluding the symbol exists and the problem is elsewhere
traps.recovery: read the matches — all are prose in comments

traps.trap: the file also calls strcpy() four times
traps.failure: replacing those too, or assuming they are equally broken

traps.trap: dkms status shows the module installed for 6.18 LTS
traps.failure: concluding DKMS or the system is broken
traps.recovery: the LTS kernel predates the removal; per-kernel build status is expected to differ

scoring.answer: fraction of golds asserted correctly; critical golds gate the item
scoring.process: fraction of required_checks performed, read from the tool transcript
scoring.headline_metric: C1 + C4 together. An agent that applies the compiler's suggestion and declares victory scores well on plausibility and zero on correctness — exactly the failure this corpus exists to measure.
